missing.title: Let's get omp installed
missing.body: visual-omp is a friendly window around omp, the AI coding agent. omp isn't on this computer yet — it takes about a minute.

tooOld.title: Your omp is out of date
tooOld.body: visual-omp needs a newer omp to work. Updating keeps your chats and settings.

done.title: omp is ready
done.body: Everything is set up. Taking you in…

step1.body: One command, runs in a window you can watch.
step1.bodyWindows: One PowerShell command, runs in a window you can watch.
step1.copyHint: Copy the install command to run it yourself in a terminal.
step1.copiedBody: Paste it into a terminal, then come back and choose Check again.
step1.running: Installing… this usually takes about a minute.
step1.failed: The installer stopped with an error (code {{code}}). You can try again, or copy the command and run it yourself.

step2.title: Check again
step2.body: Once the installer finishes, check that visual-omp can find omp.
step2.stillMissingBody: If you just installed it, try quitting and reopening visual-omp so it picks up the new install.

sidebar.title: Projects and chats
sidebar.body: Your projects and chats live here. Everything you ask for becomes a chat you can return to.

composer.title: Say what you want
composer.body: Type what you want in plain words. Enter sends. You never need commands — they're optional shortcuts.

permission.title: How much omp does on its own
permission.body: This controls how much omp does on its own. 'Auto' is a good start: it works by itself and you can always rewind.

dock.title: Watch the work
dock.body: Watch changes happen: files, diffs, previews, and helpers working in parallel.

statusbar.title: Context and cost
statusbar.body: Keep an eye on context and cost. Click anything here to learn more.

help.title: Help
help.subtitle: Short guides and the words we use.
help.noMatchesBody: omp can answer questions about itself and about your project.
help.askNeedsProjectBody: Questions go to a new chat, and chats live inside a project folder.

firstChat.title: Your first chat
firstChat.summary: Pick a folder, describe what you want, and watch omp work.
firstChat.s1: Open a project. A project is just a folder on your computer that omp works in.
firstChat.s2: Start a new chat and describe what you want in plain words, the way you'd tell a colleague.
firstChat.s3: Watch it work. Each step shows up as a card; the side panel shows the files and changes as they happen.
firstChat.s4: Keep going. Reply to refine the result, or send another message while omp is busy — it waits in line.

autoMode.title: Staying safe with Auto mode
autoMode.summary: Choose how much omp may do before asking you.
autoMode.s1: The pill under the message box sets how much omp does on its own: Ask me first, Edits OK, or Auto.
autoMode.s2: Auto lets omp edit files and run commands without asking. It's fast, and a good fit for projects you trust.
autoMode.s3: Want more control? Ask me first makes omp stop before every edit or command so you can approve it.
autoMode.s4: Mistakes are recoverable: you can always rewind a chat, and git keeps a record of every change.

rewind.title: Rewinding and forking
rewind.summary: Go back to an earlier point, or try another direction.
rewind.s1: Hover one of your messages to see Rewind and Fork.
rewind.s2: Rewind goes back to that point so you can say it differently. Everything after it is set aside, not deleted.
rewind.s3: Fork copies the chat into a new one, so you can try a different idea without losing this one.
rewind.s4: The branch tree shows every rewind and fork as a map, so you can jump between versions.

questions.title: When omp asks questions
questions.summary: Answer omp's questions and approvals right in the chat.
questions.s1: Sometimes omp needs a decision — which option to pick, or whether it may run something.
questions.s2: A question card appears in the chat, and the chat is marked in the sidebar so you don't miss it.
questions.s3: Choose an option or type your own answer. omp continues right away.
questions.s4: If you're away, visual-omp sends a notification when a chat needs your answer.

context.def: Everything omp can see at once: your messages, its replies, and the files it has read. It has a size limit.

token.def: A small chunk of text, about three-quarters of a word. Context size and cost are measured in tokens.

compaction.def: Summarizing the chat so far to free up room in the context, so the conversation can keep going.

planMode.def: omp thinks through an approach and shows you a plan to approve before it changes anything.

worktree.def: A separate copy of your project for one chat, so experiments never touch your main files.

mcp.def: A standard way to plug outside tools, like a database or ticket tracker, into omp.

agent.def: A reusable specialist omp can hand work to, like a reviewer or an explorer.

skill.def: An add-on set of instructions that teaches omp how to do a particular kind of task.

hook.def: A small script that runs automatically at certain moments, like before a command or after an edit.

subagent.def: A helper omp starts during a chat to work on part of the task in parallel.

checkpoint.def: A saved point in a chat that you can rewind to later.

tui.def: omp's own text screen in a terminal. visual-omp drives it for you behind the scenes.

modelRole.def: Which AI model does which job — everyday chat, planning, commit messages, and more.
